ocar.opportunity: Barcode sequencing can map circuits at cellular resolution and brain-wide scale at relatively low cost, but Sindbis-based methods only follow axons anterogradely. Rabies can label projection neurons retrogradely or their monosynaptic inputs.
ocar.challenge: Barcoded rabies had been used for non-neuronal interactions in vivo and for cultured synapses, not for mapping identified neuronal types in the intact mouse brain while keeping transcriptomic identity.
ocar.action: Zhang, Jin, Yao, Matsuyama, van Velthoven, Sullivan, Sun, Kellis, Tasic, Wickersham, and Chen, in an eLife reviewed preprint (this version 8 June 2023; catalog DOI 10.7554/eLife.87866), combine barcoded rabies with single-cell RNA-seq and in situ sequencing for retrograde and transsynaptic labeling in mouse cortex.
ocar.resolution: They sequenced 96 retrogradely and 295 transsynaptically labeled cells by scRNA-seq, and 4,130 retrogradely and 2,914 transsynaptically labeled cells in situ. Transcriptomic identities of infected cells were recovered with both assays. Barcodes linked gene expression to connectivity, distinguishing long-range projecting cortical types across areas and types with converging or diverging synaptic input. Retrograde labeling used two injection sites as a proof of principle.
ocar.future_work: The discussion frames multiplexed retrograde tracing from dozens of sites and multiplexed monosynaptic tracing as the next uses of barcode diversity, which is not limited by fluorescent colors.

summaries.beginner: Researchers tag mouse brain cells with barcoded rabies virus, then read both the tags and the cells’ gene activity. That pairing shows which cell types send long-range projections or share synaptic partners.
summaries.intermediate: In an eLife reviewed preprint (posted 8 June 2023), Zhang and colleagues apply barcoded rabies in the mouse brain with single-cell RNA-seq and in situ sequencing. They recover transcriptomic identity after infection and use barcodes to map retrograde projections from two sites and monosynaptic inputs. Cell counts in the extract are 96 retrograde and 295 transsynaptic cells by scRNA-seq, and 4,130 and 2,914 in situ. The method is presented as complementary to anterograde MAPseq/BARseq, which densely barcodes local somata rather than surveying projection neurons over large regions.
summaries.advanced: This is a proof-of-principle, not a brain-wide synaptic census. Retrograde multiplexity is two sites. Infected-cell transcriptomes are reported as robustly identifiable, but rabies cytotoxicity and coverage limits are not quantified in the supplied extract. Catalog year is 2024; the extract is the 2023 reviewed preprint (eLife.87866.1). In situ and scRNA-seq counts should be checked against the published Version of Record.

plain_language_summary: Researchers tag mouse brain cells with barcoded rabies virus, then read both the tags and the cells’ gene activity. That pairing shows which cell types send long-range projections or share synaptic partners.

ocar.opportunity: Primate visual cortex is modular and hierarchical, with V1 at the center, later areas encircling earlier ones, retinotopy within areas, and mirror reversals at area boundaries. A developmental rule that produces all of those features at once would explain a lot of cortical layout.
ocar.challenge: The rules that jointly create architectural, spatial, and topographic organization are unknown, and detailed genetic cues for map reversals are not established.
ocar.action: Chandra, Khona, Konkle, and Fiete, in a 8 January 2024 bioRxiv preprint, simulate a synaptic growth rule driven by spontaneous activity and heterosynaptic competition, and they name the principle local greedy wiring minimization via spontaneous drive (GWM-S).
ocar.resolution: The simulated visual-pathway connectome develops modular areas, hierarchy, and mirror reversals without detailed genetic instructions for reversals. A few parameters act as knobs that can produce projection-neuron-like versus interneuron-like connectivity. The same rules, given different input and cortical geometry, are offered as a possible explanation for pluripotent sensory-pathway formation across modalities and species.
ocar.future_work: The authors propose biologically distinct growth rules that reach similar endpoints along testably different developmental trajectories, and they list predictions for normal and perturbed development. The extract’s supplement shows robustness of d0 and γ over orders of magnitude in 1-d simulations.

summaries.beginner: A computer model grows visual-cortex wiring from simple competition among synapses. Areas, a hierarchy, and flipped maps appear without a detailed genetic blueprint for those flips.
summaries.intermediate: Chandra, Khona, Konkle, and Fiete (bioRxiv, 8 January 2024) show that spontaneous activity plus heterosynaptic competition can self-organize a visual-pathway connectome with modular areas, concentric hierarchy, retinotopy, and mirror reversals. They interpret the mechanism as local greedy wiring minimization via spontaneous drive (GWM-S). Parameters in the growth rule can shift the outcome toward projection-neuron-like or interneuron-like patterns, and input versus cortical geometry is argued to set analogous layouts in other senses.
summaries.advanced: This is a developmental simulation, not an empirical connectome. Endpoints are model-generated; biological identifiability of GWM-S versus alternative growth rules is left to future experiments. The supplied extract’s discussion is truncated into supplementary figures (parameter sweeps of d0 and γ; LGN geometry). Preprint, not peer-reviewed.

plain_language_summary: A computer model grows visual-cortex wiring from simple competition among synapses. Areas, a hierarchy, and flipped maps appear without a detailed genetic blueprint for those flips.

ocar.opportunity: Stroke is a leading cause of adult disability. Recovery depends on how brain networks reorganize across spatial and temporal scales, so a connectomics language that spans those scales could guide evaluation of remapping.
ocar.challenge: Readouts and network models have changed what is known about stroke at the macroscale, while reorganization of smaller-scale networks remains incompletely understood.
ocar.action: Latifi and Carmichael, in Trends in Neurosciences (2024), review stroke-related connectivity studies using graph theory to define brain networks from nano- to macroscales, as described in the catalog abstract.
ocar.resolution: The abstract argues that multiscale connectomics-based approaches may provide new routes to evaluate structural and functional remapping after stroke and during recovery.
ocar.future_work: How nano- and microscale network change should be measured in patients, and how those measures should be linked to macroscale imaging, is left as the review’s agenda rather than a completed protocol.

summaries.beginner: Stroke recovery is a problem of brain networks at many zoom levels, not only of a single damaged spot. This review argues that wiring-diagram ideas from the synapse up to whole-brain scans could better track how the brain remaps.
summaries.intermediate: Latifi and Carmichael (Trends in Neurosciences, 2024) review stroke damage and recovery through a graph-theory framework spanning nano- to macroscale networks. They note that macroscale connectivity is comparatively well studied, whereas smaller-scale reorganization is not, and they advocate multiscale connectomics to evaluate structural and functional remapping. Summaries here follow the catalog abstract because the associated PDF extract is a different article.
summaries.advanced: The PDF text supplied with pdf_trust=ok is Pundik et al., Brain and Behavior (2025), a cross-sectional rsFC study of sensorimotor and default-mode networks versus lower-limb performance in 37 people with chronic stroke, not the Latifi and Carmichael Trends in Neurosciences review. Numbers and claims above are taken only from the catalog abstract. Independent reading of the TINS paper is required.

plain_language_summary: Stroke recovery is a problem of brain networks at many zoom levels, not only of a single damaged spot. This review argues that wiring-diagram ideas from the synapse up to whole-brain scans could better track how the brain remaps.

ocar.opportunity: Volume electron microscopy now images large fields at high resolution by tiling overlapping frames, so a seamless mosaic is required before ultrastructure can be read.
ocar.challenge: When features are uneven and overlap matches fail, fused regions ghost. Existing stitchers struggle with mixed global rigid motion and local biological distortion.
ocar.action: He, Zhang, Zhang, Cheng, Zhang, Sun, and Han, in GigaScience (2024), introduce vEMstitch: a global rigid plus local elastic model using weighted pixel displacement fields, with local geometric constraints and feature re-extraction. They test simulated composite transforms and real vEM tiles. Code is at https://github.com/HeracleBT/vEMstitch.
ocar.resolution: On simulated combinations of transforms the method performed consistently well in the authors’ tests, and on real samples it produced clear ultrastructure in stitch regions. They argue it has broader deformation modeling than existing open-source tools for grid scans with a known path.
ocar.future_work: Limitations stated in the extract: it assumes a predetermined scanning path, cannot stitch unordered tiles, and its feature-based design has difficulty with hundreds or thousands of tiles per section. Parallelism is section-based; the rigid module can be used alone.

summaries.beginner: Volume electron microscopes take many overlapping snapshots that must be sewn together. This algorithm aims to join those tiles without blurry double images, even when the tissue itself is a bit warped.
summaries.intermediate: He and colleagues (GigaScience, 2024) present vEMstitch for automatic vEM mosaic assembly. The transform combines global rigid alignment with local elastic correction via weighted displacement fields, plus local geometric constraints and feature re-extraction meant to capture biological distortion. Simulated mixed-transform tests and real-sample stitches are reported as successful. The extract’s discussion contrasts accuracy and seamlessness with existing open-source stitchers and lists limits: known scan path, no unordered data, and poor scaling to hundreds or thousands of tiles per section.
summaries.advanced: This is a methods technical note, not a new connectome. Quantitative stitch-error tables are not in the supplied extract; claims of ‘promising’ simulation performance should be checked against the paper’s figures. λadjacent=3 and λmatching=1.5 are experimental filter settings in the extract, not biological measurements. Source code is public.

plain_language_summary: Volume electron microscopes take many overlapping snapshots that must be sewn together. This algorithm aims to join those tiles without blurry double images, even when the tissue itself is a bit warped.

ocar.opportunity: Single-neuron axon maps are needed to understand how the hippocampus broadcasts to the rest of the brain. Sparse labeling plus fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography can reconstruct somata, dendrites, and brain-wide axons.
ocar.challenge: How individual hippocampal neurons choose intra- versus extra-formation targets, and how soma position along hippocampal axes specifies those choices, had not been charted at this scale.
ocar.action: Qiu and colleagues, in Science (2024), reconstruct mouse hippocampal single-neuron projectomes and pair them with spatial transcriptomics, as described in the catalog abstract.
ocar.resolution: The abstract reports 10,100 reconstructed projectomes, 341 projection patterns grouped into 43 subtypes, target number and axon-tip placement that depend on soma location along longitudinal and transverse axes, enrichment of subtypes in transcriptomic subdomains, separate wiring diagrams for intra-HPF-only versus intra-plus-extra-HPF neurons, and a general rule that bihemispheric cells usually hit one homologous pair with ipsilateral preference.
ocar.future_work: The authors present the database as a structural basis for combining gene expression with function; specific causal tests of the new projection rules are outside the abstract.

summaries.beginner: Researchers traced the full axon trees of more than ten thousand individual mouse hippocampal neurons. The maps show that where a cell’s body sits in the hippocampus predicts where its axon goes in the brain.
summaries.intermediate: Qiu et al. (Science, 2024) combine sparse labeling with fluorescence micro-optical sectioning tomography to reconstruct 10,100 mouse hippocampal neurons, classify 43 projectome subtypes from 341 patterns, and relate soma location and spatial transcriptomic subdomains to axon targets. According to the catalog abstract, they separate intra-hippocampal-formation projections from neurons that also leave the formation, and they report that bihemispheric cells generally innervate one homologous target pair with ipsilateral bias. Summaries here follow the catalog abstract because the associated PDF extract is a different article.
summaries.advanced: The PDF text supplied with pdf_trust=ok is Vargas-Barroso, Watson, Navas-Olive, Schlögl, and Jonas, Nature Communications (2026), on developmental sparsening of mouse CA3–CA3 connectivity mapped by multicellular patch clamp, not the Qiu et al. Science hippocampal projectome. Counts (10,100 neurons, 43 subtypes, 341 patterns) are those stated in the catalog abstract. Independent reading of the Science paper is required.

plain_language_summary: Researchers traced the full axon trees of more than ten thousand individual mouse hippocampal neurons. The maps show that where a cell’s body sits in the hippocampus predicts where its axon goes in the brain.

ocar.opportunity: Volume electron microscopy can show myelin’s compacted wraps and axon–glia contacts in three dimensions, and automated segmentation can turn those volumes into quantitative morphology.
ocar.challenge: Classical TEM was the main ultrastructural tool for decades, but it does not easily yield 3-D metrics at tissue scale, while vEM datasets are large and need shared analysis pipelines.
ocar.action: Schadt, Ruhwedel, Pape, Sasmita, Steyer, and Möbius, in Methods in Microscopy (2024; received 5 August, accepted 11 November, published 16 December), review sample-preparation and analysis strategies for vEM and illustrate them with myelin biology and disease.
ocar.resolution: They argue that open vEM datasets plus automated segmentation provide quantitative cellular and organellar readouts and can be reused across questions. The review also points readers to instrumentation, methods, and software developments, including deep-learning segmentation resources cited in the reference list.
ocar.future_work: The piece is a methods-and-application review, not a new volume; it invites use of emerging tools (data-sharing efforts, BioImage Model Zoo, Segment Anything variants) in myelin and other tissues.

summaries.beginner: Myelin is a tightly wrapped insulation that is hard to see in three dimensions with ordinary electron microscopy. This review explains how volume EM and computer segmentation now measure those wraps and their diseases.
summaries.intermediate: Schadt and colleagues (Methods in Microscopy, 2024) review volume EM sample preparation, automated segmentation, and 3-D reconstruction, using myelin in the central nervous system as the application. They treat open datasets as reusable for quantitative morphology and survey new instruments and deep-learning software. Steyer and Möbius are joint last authors. The extract’s back matter is largely references (remyelination, spatial-transcriptomics-correlated EM, FIB-SEM, data sharing).
summaries.advanced: This is a narrative methods review, not a new reconstruction. The supplied extract does not include a single quantitative myelin metric from the authors’ own volumes. Claims about disease insight should be traced to the cited primary papers. Supplementary material is linked at the journal DOI.

plain_language_summary: Myelin is a tightly wrapped insulation that is hard to see in three dimensions with ordinary electron microscopy. This review explains how volume EM and computer segmentation now measure those wraps and their diseases.

ocar.opportunity: Whole-brain network analysis began in the 1980s with a handful of connectomes and no human maps. Non-invasive diffusion imaging and related methods now supply structural connectivity in many species and many individuals.
ocar.challenge: Making scientific use of that abundance—comparing organization across species, and moving from one animal to populations—is a different problem from having no data at all.
ocar.action: Kaiser, in Frontiers in Neuroinformatics (published 12 June 2023), reviews available structural connectome data, shared organizational features, and current challenges.
ocar.resolution: He notes that the UK Biobank is on track to record structural and functional connectivity in 100,000 human subjects, and that maps now exist from C. elegans and fruit fly through pigeons, rodents, cats, non-human primates, and humans. The conclusion states that over about 15 years, major databases have given at least one individual connectome for many mammalian and invertebrate species, with human efforts expanding beyond Western samples (e.g., Chinese databases) and across the lifespan. Partial maps (leech, tadpole, mouse retina) are distinguished from whole-brain resources.
ocar.future_work: The review closes on using connectome information scientifically—disease progression and early biomarkers in longitudinal UK Biobank dementia data are given as examples—rather than on a single new analysis.

summaries.beginner: Thirty years ago almost no whole-brain wiring diagrams existed. This review surveys the flood of maps now available, from worms and flies to a planned 100,000 human scans.
summaries.intermediate: Kaiser (Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 2023) reviews the shift from a few 1980s connectomes to large structural-connectivity databases. Diffusion imaging is credited for multi-species and multi-individual coverage. The UK Biobank target of 100,000 structural and functional scans is used to illustrate scale. Shared organizational features across species are promised in the abstract; the extract’s conclusion emphasizes population imaging, broader geography, lifespan data, and leftover partial nervous-system maps (leech, tadpole, mouse retina).
summaries.advanced: This is a narrative review of data availability, not a new reconstruction or a quantitative meta-analysis of motif frequencies. The 100,000 UK Biobank figure is a stated trajectory, not a completed release count in the extract. Species coverage is illustrative. Catalog tags include C. elegans (White+); the review is multi-species.

plain_language_summary: Thirty years ago almost no whole-brain wiring diagrams existed. This review surveys the flood of maps now available, from worms and flies to a planned 100,000 human scans.

ocar.opportunity: Biological connectomes contain cycles. Turning a recurrent network into a directed acyclic graph can reduce computational load and make sensory-to-neuromuscular pathways easier to read as feedforward chains.
ocar.challenge: Cycle-breaking must not destroy the architecture one cares about. Different algorithms delete different edges.
ocar.action: Li, in the 2023 IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference, customizes depth-first search (DFS) and minimum feedback arc set (MFAS) to remove cycles in the C. elegans adult hermaphrodite connectome, then scores retained edges, sensory-to-neuromuscular-junction pathways, and other graph properties.
ocar.resolution: The abstract reports that MFAS retains the structural authenticity of the original graph significantly better than DFS. Mentorship acknowledgements name Constantine Dovrolis and Ross Greer.
ocar.future_work: How these DAGs should be used for simulation or pathway ranking, and how well the result generalizes beyond the hermaphrodite chemical-synapse graph, is outside the extract.

summaries.beginner: The worm’s wiring diagram has loops. This student paper tries two algorithms that cut loops so the network becomes a one-way flowchart, and reports that one method keeps the original shape better.
summaries.intermediate: Li (IEEE MIT URTC, 2023) applies customized DFS and MFAS cycle-breaking to the adult hermaphrodite C. elegans connectome. Evaluation uses edges kept, sensory-neuron-to-NMJ pathways, and other graphical properties. The abstract concludes that MFAS preserves structural authenticity significantly better than DFS. The extract notes that feedforward views can lower computational load and clarify downstream pathways.
summaries.advanced: This is an undergraduate conference paper, not a new reconstruction. Quantitative edge-retention or pathway counts are not in the supplied extract (front matter plus references). ‘Structural authenticity’ is the author’s comparative claim for MFAS versus DFS. Licensed IEEE Xplore PDF; White et al. 1986 and Varshney et al. 2011 appear in the reference list as source connectomes.

plain_language_summary: The worm’s wiring diagram has loops. This student paper tries two algorithms that cut loops so the network becomes a one-way flowchart, and reports that one method keeps the original shape better.

ocar.opportunity: In early retinal degeneration, bipolar cells still receive photoreceptor input. Stimulating them with a prosthesis might restore more naturalistic signals than waiting until only inner retina remains.
ocar.challenge: How degeneration changes bipolar-cell responses to extracellular current is not obvious from late-stage devices, and ON versus OFF cone bipolar cells may not behave the same way.
ocar.action: Farzad, Kosta, Iseri, Walston, Bouteiller, Pfeiffer, Sigulinsky, Yang, Garcia, Anderson, Jones, and Lazzi, in IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering (2023), build computational models of healthy and early-degenerate ON and OFF cone bipolar cells using realistic morphologies from healthy and early-stage degenerated rabbit retina connectomes, then apply electrical stimuli while varying pulse duration and electrode distance.
ocar.resolution: OFF CBC membrane potential did not differ significantly between healthy and degenerate cells regardless of position in the model. Healthy ON CBC axon-terminal membrane-potential rising time-constant was shorter (0.29 ± 0.03 ms) than in degenerated cells (0.8 ± 0.07 ms). Axon-terminal calcium current was higher in degenerated cells (32.24 ± 6.12 pA) than in healthy cells (13.64 ± 2.88 pA), independent of cell position.
ocar.future_work: The models address early-stage rabbit CBC biophysics under stimulation; translation to human RP/AMD prostheses and to other bipolar classes is not settled in the extract.

summaries.beginner: Eye implants usually wait until photoreceptors are gone. This study models how remaining bipolar cells in a degenerating rabbit retina respond to electrical pulses, and finds ON and OFF cells do not change in the same way.
summaries.intermediate: Farzad et al. (IEEE TNSRE, 2023) simulate healthy versus early-degenerate ON and OFF cone bipolar cells whose morphologies come from rabbit retina connectomes. Electrical stimulation is varied by pulse duration and electrode distance. OFF CBC membrane potentials are reported as not significantly different after degeneration. ON CBC axon-terminal voltage rises more slowly after degeneration (0.29 ± 0.03 vs 0.8 ± 0.07 ms), and terminal calcium current is larger in degenerate cells (32.24 ± 6.12 vs 13.64 ± 2.88 pA), independent of position.
summaries.advanced: These are NEURON-style biophysical models constrained by connectome morphologies, not new EM or in vivo stimulation. Species in the paper is rabbit; catalog organism tags list mouse. Uncertainties are those reported (±) in the abstract. ‘Not a significant difference’ for OFF CBCs is the authors’ statistical claim; test details are not in the extract. Calcium-channel ‘higher concentration and higher current’ should be read as model ionic current, not a measured protein assay.

plain_language_summary: Eye implants usually wait until photoreceptors are gone. This study models how remaining bipolar cells in a degenerating rabbit retina respond to electrical pulses, and finds ON and OFF cells do not change in the same way.

ocar.opportunity: A complete fly optic-lobe wiring diagram lets one ask what insects see of form, a question long studied in behavior but neglected relative to motion and color in physiology.
ocar.challenge: Form vision must be inferred from anatomy until the relevant cells are recorded. Preferred orientation is not yet measured for the types under study.
ocar.action: Seung, in a 15 November 2023 bioRxiv preprint, interprets a Drosophila optic-lobe connectome, focusing on three Dm3 ‘line amacrine’ types with oriented dendrites and three connected TmY types, also with oriented dendrites.
ocar.resolution: All six types are predicted to be orientation-selective with preference matching dendrite orientation. Receptive fields are predicted from inputs that mainly convey single-facet information. Dm3→Dm3 and Dm3→TmY connectivity is approximated as cross-orientation inhibition and TmY→TmY as iso-orientation excitation—motifs hypothesized for mammalian visual cortex. Two TmY types target a novel LC10 type leading toward visual-form learning centers. Spatial organization of TmY–TmY and LC10 connections grounds a conjecture that flies may see illusory contours and corners. TmY4 receives T4/T5 motion input expected to enhance orientation selectivity for moving versus flashed stimuli.
ocar.future_work: Visual responses remain unmeasured, so orientation-selectivity and illusory-contour claims are predictions. The extract contrasts the completeness of fly proofs with the still-small number of fully proofread MICrONS cortical neurons.

summaries.beginner: A wiring diagram of the fruit-fly optic lobe is used to guess how flies see shapes, not just motion or color. Some cells look built to prefer lines at particular angles, a trick also discussed for mammalian visual cortex.
summaries.intermediate: Seung (bioRxiv, 15 November 2023) analyzes Drosophila optic-lobe connectivity among three Dm3 types and three TmY types with oriented dendrites. He predicts orientation selectivity from dendrite geometry and single-facet inputs, describes Dm3 cross-orientation inhibition and TmY iso-orientation excitation, and notes a novel LC10 target of two TmY types on paths toward form-learning neuropils. Illusory contours and corners are conjectures from spatial connectivity. Motion-form crosstalk is discussed via TmY4’s T4/T5 input.
summaries.advanced: This is an interpretive preprint, not new EM or physiology. ‘Orientation’ in the connectivity motifs refers first to dendritic structure; preferred visual orientation is explicitly unmeasured. Deviations from idealized motifs (off-diagonal TmY→TmY; TmY9q⟂ onto all Dm3 types) are acknowledged. Illusory-contour language is a conjecture. Compare to later peer-reviewed versions before treating predictions as results.

plain_language_summary: A wiring diagram of the fruit-fly optic lobe is used to guess how flies see shapes, not just motion or color. Some cells look built to prefer lines at particular angles, a trick also discussed for mammalian visual cortex.

ocar.opportunity: Topological data analysis reports high Betti numbers in microscale connectomes. A null model that keeps the undirected graph and roughly the same simplex counts can test whether that topology is more than a side effect of many cliques.
ocar.challenge: Uniform sampling of directed graphs with those constraints is hard. Mixing, rejection rates, and even irreducibility of the Markov chain are not trivial.
ocar.action: Unger and Krebs (manuscript dated 5 September 2023; journal Journal of Applied and Computational Topology) define such a null model, give an MCMC sampler with a public Rust implementation, study mixing statistically, and apply it to the C. elegans connectome and parts of Blue Brain Project statistical reconstructions.
ocar.resolution: Observed Betti numbers are reported as considerable statistical outliers relative to this null, which the authors take as the first statistical confirmation that TDA on microscale connectomes extracts meaningful information rather than simplex-count artifacts.
ocar.future_work: They lack rigorous proofs of irreducibility in the double-edge case; sampling small, large, or locally dense graphs is expensive (weeks to months). They want better rejection bounds, tests of q-connectedness and simplex completion probability, and application to the full BBP connectome and Drosophila larva.

summaries.beginner: Fancy shape statistics on brain wiring diagrams can look impressive just because there are many little cliques. This paper builds a fair random comparison and finds the worm and some simulated cortical networks are still unusual.
summaries.intermediate: Unger and Krebs introduce a uniformly sampleable null model of directed graphs that preserve the undirected skeleton and similar flag-complex simplex counts, with an MCMC sampler (Rust, public). Applied to C. elegans and portions of Blue Brain Project statistical reconstructions, Betti numbers of the real/reconstructed graphs are outliers versus the null. The discussion flags unproven irreducibility for double-edge graphs, high computational cost, and planned scaling to denser connectomes.
summaries.advanced: Outlier status is with respect to this specific null (fixed undirected graph, constrained simplex counts), not all possible configuration models. The authors note that even without irreducibility the unusual-topology claim would still hold inside the sampled connected component. Catalog year is 2023; the DOI is a 2024 journal record. Mixing-time proofs are absent; estimated step counts of order c·s1 log(s1) appear as computational remarks, not biological measurements.

plain_language_summary: Fancy shape statistics on brain wiring diagrams can look impressive just because there are many little cliques. This paper builds a fair random comparison and finds the worm and some simulated cortical networks are still unusual.

ocar.opportunity: Telencephalic computation is shaped not only by synapses but by neuromodulators that act through distributed connections and volume transmission. A molecular map of cell types and GPCRs would constrain that chemistry in adult zebrafish.
ocar.challenge: Which combinations of monoamines and neuropeptides address which cell types, and with what relative weights, is not obvious from anatomy alone.
ocar.action: Anneser, Satou, Hotz, and Friedrich, in Current Biology (2023), use transcriptomics and additional approaches to delineate cell types, assess phylogenetic conservation, and map marker genes at high granularity, as described in the catalog abstract.
ocar.resolution: The abstract reports that combinatorial GPCR and cell-type marker expression implies every neuronal type is modulated by multiple monoaminergic systems and distinct neuropeptide combinations. Individual types associate with many (typically >30) neuromodulatory networks but express only a few diagnostic GPCRs at high levels, suggesting combined action with unequal weights.
ocar.future_work: The abstract presents the map as a starting point for the logic of combinatorial neuromodulation, not as a complete physiological test of co-release or volume-transmission reach.

summaries.beginner: In the adult zebrafish forebrain, every neuron type seems to listen to several chemical broadcast systems at once, but a few receptors are much louder than the rest.
summaries.intermediate: Anneser, Satou, Hotz, and Friedrich (Current Biology, 2023) map neuronal cell types and neuromodulatory systems in the adult zebrafish telencephalon. According to the catalog abstract, all neuronal types appear subject to multiple monoamines and neuropeptides; types typically participate in more than 30 neuromodulatory networks while expressing only a few GPCRs at high level. Summaries follow the abstract because the associated PDF extract is supplemental material rather than the main narrative.
summaries.advanced: The PDF extract is Current Biology Supplemental Information for this article (Figures S1–S2: pallial bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq quality versus Cosacak, Raj, and Spanjaard datasets; Table S1 of GPCR bulk expression), not the main text. Numbers such as typically >30 networks are from the catalog abstract. Independent reading of the article is required for phylogenetic conservation, spatial maps, and statistics.

plain_language_summary: In the adult zebrafish forebrain, every neuron type seems to listen to several chemical broadcast systems at once, but a few receptors are much louder than the rest.

ocar.opportunity: Female Drosophila change song responses after hearing conspecific courtship song, a compact model of experience-dependent auditory plasticity. GABAergic input to pC1 neurons is required, but the source of that GABA was unknown.
ocar.challenge: pC1 integrates multimodal and internal state signals for mating; identifying the GABAergic partners and their modulators is needed to explain how prior song experience alters copulation.
ocar.action: Imoto, Ishikawa, Aso, Funke, Tanaka, and Kamikouchi, in iScience (published 13 June 2024; catalog year 2023), combine behavior, RNAi, immunohistochemistry, and FlyEM synapse detection.
ocar.resolution: They identify pCd-2 neurons—four cells per hemibrain, doublesex-positive—as the GABAergic source to pC1 needed for song preference learning. Knockdown of GABA production in pCd-2 abolishes learning. pCd-2 and pC1 are directly and often mutually connected. GABAergic and dopaminergic inputs to pCd-2 are both necessary, with GABA and dopamine contributing differentially. Highlights frame a reciprocal pC1–pCd-2 hub.
ocar.future_work: How dopamine and GABA onto pCd-2 encode the memory itself, and how the motif generalizes beyond song, is left open. The authors disclose ChatGPT use for language editing.

summaries.beginner: Female fruit flies learn which courtship songs to prefer. This paper finds a tiny pair of cell types in the brain that inhibit each other and need both GABA and dopamine for that learning.
summaries.intermediate: Imoto et al. (iScience 27, 110266, 19 July 2024 issue; received 28 November 2023) show that doublesex-positive pCd-2 neurons (four per hemibrain) supply GABA to pC1 for Drosophila song preference learning. RNAi against GABA synthesis in pCd-2 blocks learning; EM connectivity (FlyEM) shows reciprocal pC1–pCd-2 synapses; GABA and dopamine inputs to pCd-2 are required and contribute differentially. Behavior uses training, sound playback, and copulation tests with an AFT statistical model.
summaries.advanced: Catalog metadata list bioRxiv 2023; the extract is the peer-reviewed iScience paper. ‘Four cells per hemibrain’ is from the abstract. Synapses are database-detected, not a new EM volume. Causal claims rest on intersectional genetics and knockdown, not on closed-loop physiology of the full motif during learning. Generative-AI language editing is declared.

plain_language_summary: Female fruit flies learn which courtship songs to prefer. This paper finds a tiny pair of cell types in the brain that inhibit each other and need both GABA and dopamine for that learning.

ocar.opportunity: Animals must tell self-generated sensory signals from external ones. Predictive motor signals from motor to sensory pathways can do that, but their cellular and synaptic architecture is poorly known.
ocar.challenge: Single sensors cannot label a cue as reafferent versus exafferent. Corollary discharge and efference copy are related ideas that need circuit-level definitions.
ocar.action: Cheong, Boone, Bennett, Salman, Ralston, Hatch, Allen, Phelps, Cook, Phelps, Erginkaya, Lee, Card, Daly, and Dacks, in a 9 June 2023 bioRxiv preprint, reconstruct two pairs of ascending histaminergic neurons (AHNs) in male and female fly EM volumes, with transcriptomics, anatomy, physiology, and behavior.
ocar.resolution: Both AHN pairs receive overlapping descending input, much of it from wing-related descending neurons (a large share from DNg02s; shared DNp54s). The pairs tile almost non-overlapping outputs onto visual, auditory, and mechanosensory networks and onto wing, haltere, and leg motor circuits. AHNs become active during flight. The authors assign MsAHNs a corollary-discharge-like role to visual motion circuits (and feedforward flight circuitry in the VNC) and MtAHNs a mix of VNC corollary discharge to leg networks and brain efference copy to auditory afferents and first-order auditory interneurons. They present this as the first documented VNC-to-brain ascending pathway for flight motor state.
ocar.future_work: Functions of additional DN inputs remain unknown. Parallel flight-state pathways to visual circuits are acknowledged; AHNs are not claimed to be the only route.

summaries.beginner: When a fly beats its wings, its own sensors are flooded with self-made signals. Two pairs of histaminergic cells carry a copy of flight motor commands up to the brain so sensory circuits can tell self from world.
summaries.intermediate: Cheong et al. (bioRxiv, 9 June 2023) map two pairs of ascending histaminergic neurons (AHNs) with male and female EM connectomes plus physiology. Shared descending inputs are largely flight-related (including DNg02 and DNp54). Outputs of the two pairs barely overlap, targeting distinct sensory and motor neuropils. MsAHNs are interpreted as corollary discharge to visual motion circuits; MtAHNs as corollary discharge in the VNC and efference copy in audition. AHNs fire during flight, similar to Manduca.
summaries.advanced: This is a preprint combining connectomics and physiology. CDC versus efference-copy labels are interpretive, following cited reviews. ‘First documented ascending flight-state pathway’ is the authors’ claim relative to previously known descending and brain-intrinsic routes. Proofreading acknowledgements indicate community EM tracing. Catalog organism field is empty; the work is Drosophila.

plain_language_summary: When a fly beats its wings, its own sensors are flooded with self-made signals. Two pairs of histaminergic cells carry a copy of flight motor commands up to the brain so sensory circuits can tell self from world.

ocar.opportunity: Sugar taste drives feeding, locomotion, place preference, and learning. Knowing where those behaviors split in the circuit would show how one cue yields many actions.
ocar.challenge: It is unclear whether sugar-evoked behaviors are coordinately modulated and at which layer a five-layer feeding circuit diverges into other pathways.
ocar.action: Jacobs, Wang, Lozada-Perdomo, Nguyen, Deere, Uttley, and Devineni, in a 2 October 2023 bioRxiv preprint, optogenetically activate sugar-sensing neurons while measuring locomotion, spatial preference, and associative learning, then manipulate identified feeding-circuit layers and use connectomics.
ocar.resolution: Hunger, diet, and aversive taste generally modulate the behaviors similarly, with exceptions that imply selective pathway control. Innate sugar responses diverge at second- and third-order neurons; innate versus learned behaviors may split at the first synapse. Bitter activation dominates coincident sugar activation. High-intensity Gr64f-Gal4 stimulation can reverse innate preference to avoidance, which the authors treat as possibly unnatural recruitment of aversive subsets; downstream Rattle and FMIn did not produce that aversion.
ocar.future_work: How bitter gates sugar at the circuit level is named as an open question. Hunger affects sugar behaviors more than bitter locomotion/preference, matching ethology.

summaries.beginner: Sugar makes flies eat, slow down, linger, and remember places. This study asks whether those reactions share one circuit or split apart, and finds the split starts a synapse or two downstream of the sensors.
summaries.intermediate: Jacobs et al. (bioRxiv, 2 October 2023) use optogenetic activation of Drosophila sugar neurons to assay locomotion, positional preference, and learning, then test modulation by hunger, diet, and bitter. Innate behaviors diverge at second- and third-order neurons of a published five-layer feeding circuit; learned versus innate paths may diverge at the first synapse. Connectomic subcircuits are reported. Bitter dominates sugar when both are activated. Strong Gr64f-Gal4 drive can invert preference, unlike natural high sucrose concentrations.
summaries.advanced: Preprint. Optogenetic intensity is not equivalent to sugar concentration; the authors discuss this caveat explicitly. Catalog author list includes Pruitt, Panxi Wang, and Liphart, who are not on the preprint author line in the extract—use the PDF authors for citation. Divergence ‘may’ split at the first synapse is hedged in the abstract. No new EM volume; analyses use existing connectivity.

plain_language_summary: Sugar makes flies eat, slow down, linger, and remember places. This study asks whether those reactions share one circuit or split apart, and finds the split starts a synapse or two downstream of the sensors.

ocar.opportunity: Self-organized criticality is often inferred in large networks from avalanches. A small nervous system still needs a test of whether activity sits at a critical branching point.
ocar.challenge: C. elegans has 302 neurons, too few for avalanche methods. Branching-parameter approaches have been proposed instead.
ocar.action: Gu, Liu, Yuan, Zhao, Xin, and Fang, in the Proceedings of the 42nd Chinese Control Conference (Tianjin, 24–26 July 2023), build a directed-graph model from the C. elegans connectome to simulate gradient potentials and activity, compute a branching parameter, and compare to experimental calcium activity.
ocar.resolution: They report that the branching parameter indicates self-organized criticality, that simulated over-excitation or abnormal stages lose it, and that calcium data keep a stable number of ‘excited’ neurons by their threshold, which they treat as confirmation.
ocar.future_work: They suggest the result will help analyze information processing in other small biological networks. Catalog venue metadata list a different conference name than the PDF header.

summaries.beginner: Big brains are sometimes said to hover at a knife-edge between quiet and chaos. This conference paper asks whether the tiny worm nervous system sits at that same edge, using a simple activity-spreading number instead of large avalanches.
summaries.intermediate: Gu et al. (42nd Chinese Control Conference, 2023) argue that avalanche statistics are unsuitable for the 302-neuron C. elegans network and instead use a branching parameter on a directed-graph simulation of the connectome, with a second check on experimental calcium activity. They conclude the network is at self-organized criticality and that simulated over-excitation destroys it. Calcium traces are described as maintaining a stable count of excited neurons under their definition.
summaries.advanced: This is a conference proceedings paper, not a new connectome. ‘Proved’ in the abstract is the authors’ wording; branching-parameter equality to one is a model-dependent criterion. How chemical versus gap-junction edges and polarity were assigned should be checked in the methods. Catalog journal field says Cybersecurity and Cyberforensics Conference; the PDF is CCC 2023. Do not treat SOC as independently verified from this extract alone.

plain_language_summary: Big brains are sometimes said to hover at a knife-edge between quiet and chaos. This conference paper asks whether the tiny worm nervous system sits at that same edge, using a simple activity-spreading number instead of large avalanches.

ocar.opportunity: Vision encodes object location on the retina, but actions must be aimed in body coordinates. How that coordinate change is implemented at synapses is largely unknown.
ocar.challenge: Feature-detecting visual projection neurons (VPNs) have topographic dendrites; their axons often lack matching topography, so location must be written some other way onto premotor neurons.
ocar.action: Dombrovski, Peek, Park, Vaccari, Sumathipala, Morrow, Breads, Zhao, Kurmangaliyev, Sanfilippo, Rehan, Polsky, Alghailani, Tenshaw, Namiki, Zipursky, and Card, in Nature (published 4 January 2023; accepted 11 November 2022), combine Drosophila behavior, physiology, anatomy, and connectomics.
ocar.resolution: They show visuomotor transformation by converting dendritic topographic maps into synaptic-weight gradients of VPN outputs onto central brain neurons. Two neurons postsynaptic to a looming-responsive VPN type promote opposite takeoff directions; opposite weight gradients from VPNs in different visual-field regions convert localized looms into correctly oriented escapes. A second looming VPN type shows graded responses along the dorsoventral axis. The gradient motif is reported across all 20 primary VPN cell types, most often without VPN axon topography.
ocar.future_work: Whether synaptic gradients are a general solution in other species and modalities is posed as a mechanistic hypothesis from the fly data.

summaries.beginner: To jump away from a threat, a fly must turn retinal location into a body-centered escape. This Nature paper shows that the mapping is written as graded synapse strengths, not as a second picture in the axons.
summaries.intermediate: Dombrovski et al. (Nature, 2023) show in Drosophila that VPN dendritic topography is transformed into synaptic-weight gradients onto central neurons. For looming, two postsynaptic cells drive opposite takeoff directions via opposite LC4-type gradients (DNp02, DNp11, DNp04 appear in extract figure panels). A second looming VPN varies along the dorsoventral axis. The authors report the motif in all 20 primary VPN types, usually without axonal topography. Methods combine behavior, physiology, anatomy, and connectomics.
summaries.advanced: ‘All 20 primary VPN cell types’ is the paper’s claim; exceptions would be in the figures. Catalog datasets tag mouse retina, which does not match this fly study. P-values in the extract figure (e.g., 3.0×10⁻¹¹) belong to specific panels and should not be cited without the figure. Open-access Nature article; received 13 May 2022.

plain_language_summary: To jump away from a threat, a fly must turn retinal location into a body-centered escape. This Nature paper shows that the mapping is written as graded synapse strengths, not as a second picture in the axons.

ocar.opportunity: Neurological disease burden is rising. Massive, diverse datasets and heavier compute are starting to change neuroscience and neurology, including connectomics and several clinical domains.
ocar.challenge: Many studies labeled Big Data do not satisfy classic 3V/5V definitions, so they underuse AI methods suited to heterogeneous, high-velocity clinical data.
ocar.action: Dipietro, Gonzalez-Mego, Ramos-Estebanez, Zukowski, Mikkilineni, Rushmore, and Wagner, in Journal of Big Data (2023), survey Big Data work in connectomics, Alzheimer’s disease, stroke, depression, Parkinson’s disease, pain, and addiction (including opioid use disorder), reviewing methods, limits, and technical challenges.
ocar.resolution: They report reviewing over 300 papers and 120 databases. The full potential of Big Data in these fields is described as unrealized. Recommendations include standardizing the 5Vs, multi-center volume, wearable velocity, data variety, harmonization for veracity, explicit value, and training.
ocar.future_work: The closing agenda is to make studies actually Big Data in the 5V sense so that AI methods can personalize treatment of heterogeneous neurological disorders.

summaries.beginner: Neurology is gathering huge piles of scans and records, but this survey says much of that work is not truly ‘big data’ yet. Better sharing, faster home measures, and clearer standards could change patient care.
summaries.intermediate: Dipietro et al. (Journal of Big Data, 2023) survey Big Data in neuroscience and neurology across connectomics and several diseases. They frame the literature with 3V/5V definitions and conclude that many studies miss velocity, variety, or veracity and therefore rarely use characteristic AI methods. Their review of over 300 papers and 120 databases ends with recommendations: standardize Vs, grow multi-center volume, use wearables, diversify data types, harmonize, score value, and train researchers.
summaries.advanced: This is a literature survey, not a new dataset or algorithm. ‘Over 300 papers and 120 databases’ is the authors’ count as of their search; inclusion criteria are in the full methods. Clinical-impact claims are prospective. Connectomics appears as one surveyed area among others.

plain_language_summary: Neurology is gathering huge piles of scans and records, but this survey says much of that work is not truly ‘big data’ yet. Better sharing, faster home measures, and clearer standards could change patient care.

ocar.opportunity: Complete single-neuron reconstructions now let one convert thalamic axons into meso-scale projection statistics instead of stopping at individual pretty trees.
ocar.challenge: Linking topography, higher-order projection motifs, and morphological diversity in one workflow is still hard, even for a well-studied nucleus such as VPM.
ocar.action: Timonidis, Bakker, Rubio-Teves, Alonso-Martínez, García-Amado, Clascá, and Tiesinga, in Frontiers in Neuroinformatics (published 1 December 2023), analyze 257 mouse VPM neurons from MouseLight and Braintell, cluster them by dominant and joint cortical targets, and embed axonal-tree dissimilarities.
ocar.resolution: A curved 2-D embedding collapses to a 1-D coordinate aligned with soma position along dorsal–ventral and lateral–medial axes, with axonal terminals along posterior–anterior and medial–lateral axes, and with increases in branch points, distance from soma, and branching width. Projection motifs span monofocal and multifocal output along a spectrum from primary somatosensory mouth toward supplemental, nose, and barrel cortex. They release a portal for visualizing on the order of 10,000 fully reconstructed neurons, with Python access.
ocar.future_work: The workflow is offered for modeling and experimental tests of thalamocortical hypotheses beyond this VPM case.

summaries.beginner: Thousands of traced mouse neurons sit in public databases. This team turns 257 sensory-thalamus cells into a simple map: where the cell body sits predicts the shape of its axon and which cortical patches it hits.
summaries.intermediate: Timonidis et al. (Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 2023) combine 257 VPM reconstructions from MouseLight and Braintell. Clustering is by dominant and co-targeted cortical areas; morphological diversity is a pairwise axonal-tree dissimilarity embedding whose curved manifold yields a 1-D coordinate aligned with soma and terminal topography and with branching statistics. A community portal visualizes reconstructions on the order of 10,000 neurons on cortical flatmaps. Funding includes FLAG-ERA NeuronsReunited and HBP SGA3.
summaries.advanced: n=257 VPM cells; the ‘order of 10,000’ figure is the portal’s broader reconstruction collection, not the VPM sample. Embedding alignments are reported as observed correspondences, not as proven causal maps. This reanalyzes public morphologies rather than acquiring a new volume.

plain_language_summary: Thousands of traced mouse neurons sit in public databases. This team turns 257 sensory-thalamus cells into a simple map: where the cell body sits predicts the shape of its axon and which cortical patches it hits.

ocar.opportunity: Sex differences in behavior are often credited to sex-specific neurons. Sex-shared neurons that exist in both C. elegans sexes can also rewire or change function, offering a second route to dimorphic circuits.
ocar.challenge: Dimorphism can appear as neurite shape change with new synapses, as synapse change without obvious shape change, or as functional modulation with little connectivity change—and the molecular control is not a single switch.
ocar.action: Kim and Kim, in a Frontiers in Neuroanatomy mini-review (published 6 May 2022), synthesize anatomical and functional differences in sex-shared worm neurons and the roles of TRA-1, DMD transcription factors, and neural cell-surface proteins.
ocar.resolution: Examples include dimorphic neurite branching and connectivity, cryptic synaptic differences, and modulation such as AWA ODR-10 (food detection, high in hermaphrodites via TRA-1) versus SRD-1 (male pheromone attraction). TRA-1 expression among sex-shared neurons varies with age, sex, and environment. The authors argue that combining connectomics, developmental genetics, and behavior will explain how sex differences arise and why some human neurological disorders show sex bias.
ocar.future_work: They call for comprehensive studies that join those levels, including environmental modulation of TRA-1.

summaries.beginner: Male and female worms share most of the same neurons, yet those shared cells can grow extra branches, make different synapses, or simply work differently. This short review collects those tricks and the genes behind them.
summaries.intermediate: Kim and Kim (Frontiers in Neuroanatomy, 2022) review sex-shared C. elegans neurons. They classify dimorphisms as morphological (neurite projection/branching with connectivity change), synaptic without obvious structure change, and functional with little connectivity change. Molecular control is framed through TRA-1 and DMD factors regulating effectors such as cell-surface proteins, with AWA ODR-10 and SRD-1 as receptor examples. Recent work showing variable TRA-1 among shared neurons is emphasized.
summaries.advanced: Mini-review of published connectomic and genetic studies, not new EM. Human sex-bias in disease is an analogy in the closing paragraph, not a result. Catalog dataset tag is C. elegans (White+); much of the cited dimorphism literature post-dates the original hermaphrodite map.

plain_language_summary: Male and female worms share most of the same neurons, yet those shared cells can grow extra branches, make different synapses, or simply work differently. This short review collects those tricks and the genes behind them.

ocar.opportunity: Large-volume SEM is too slow at full dose and full pixel coverage. Low-dose sparse scans can be computationally inpainted if reconstruction keeps up with acquisition.
ocar.challenge: Classical reconstructors such as GOAL are too heavy for live use, and high-dose full-frame ground truth is often spoiled by drift, damage, and charging.
ocar.action: De Putter, Peemen, Potocek, Schoenmakers, and Corporaal, in the 2022 25th Euromicro Conference on Digital System Design (IEEE; published 4 January 2023 in the repository record), propose CELR: CNNs approximate GOAL locally for delayed-live reconstruction, while recurring CNN training and GOAL label generation run in the cloud. They optimize throughput with NVIDIA TensorRT.
ocar.resolution: The combination of CELR and TensorRT is reported to reconstruct large-volume acquisitions with 1 μs dwell time and 10% pixel coverage on a single GPU. Training can use noise-to-noise pairs when clean references are unavailable.
ocar.future_work: The paper flags open questions about on-the-fly CNN training. Sample drift still limits high-dose evaluation references.

summaries.beginner: Electron microscopes can scan faster if they skip most pixels and use a faint beam, but then a computer must fill in the picture. This system splits the work: a local neural net reconstructs live, while the cloud keeps training the net.
summaries.intermediate: De Putter et al. (Euromicro DSD 2022 / IEEE) present CELR for reconstructing low-dose sparse SEM. Local CNNs approximate GOAL; cloud jobs regenerate labels and retrain. TensorRT is used to raise reconstruction throughput. They report that 1 μs dwell and 10% coverage volumes can be reconstructed on one GPU. Noise-to-noise training is discussed when high-dose full frames are impractical because of drift, damage, or charging.
summaries.advanced: Conference methods paper. Image-quality metrics versus GOAL are not in the supplied extract (repository cover plus paper tail/references). 1 μs and 10% coverage are the authors’ stated operating point, not a biological resolution. Catalog year 2022 matches the conference; the TU/e record lists 4 January 2023. Taverne license on the repository copy.

plain_language_summary: Electron microscopes can scan faster if they skip most pixels and use a faint beam, but then a computer must fill in the picture. This system splits the work: a local neural net reconstructs live, while the cloud keeps training the net.

ocar.opportunity: Fly olfactory projection neurons are transcriptomically diverse. Whether their boutons are equally diverse in ultrastructure—and thus in transmitter versus neuromodulator release capacity—was unknown.
ocar.challenge: Bouton shape, presynaptic active zones (PAZs), and dense-core vesicles (DCVs) need volumetric EM quantification, not light-level morphology.
ocar.action: Yang, Liu, Wang, Liu, Shen, Pan, Wen, Xie, Ruan, Tan, Chen, Guo, Liu, Han, Di, and Zhang, in iScience (20 May 2022), volumetrically reconstruct 89 PN boutons from FIB-SEM and cluster them on internal PAZ and DCV measurements, with a GH146-labeled subset.
ocar.resolution: Three morphological subtypes appear: complex, unilobed, and simple. Complex boutons hold the most PAZs and DCVs, interpreted as the highest combined release capacity. PAZ number scales linearly with bouton size. DCVs are preferentially found in certain GH146-positive subtypes. The imaged block is 20 × 20 × 25 μm, about 1/30 of the mushroom-body main calyx, from one sample.
ocar.future_work: The authors say generalization across individuals needs more samples or DCV annotation in TEMCA2 and Hemibrain, where all PNs are identified; GH146 labels about two-thirds of PNs, so subtype-specific DCV claims remain coarse.

summaries.beginner: Olfactory neurons in the fly dump smell information into the learning center at swollen axon endings. Electron-microscope reconstructions split those endings into three shapes, and the most elaborate ones look best equipped to release both fast transmitters and slower chemical modulators.
summaries.intermediate: Yang et al. (iScience, 2022) reconstruct 89 Drosophila PN boutons with FIB-SEM and quantify PAZs and DCVs. Clustering yields complex, unilobed, and simple boutons; complex boutons have the most of both organelles. PAZ count is linearly related to bouton size. DCVs prefer GH146-positive boutons. The volume is 20×20×25 μm (~1/30 of main calyx) from one animal. Limitations include single-sample scope and incomplete PN-type identity for DCV enrichment.
summaries.advanced: n=89 boutons, one calyx fragment. ‘Highest capability of releasing’ is an ultrastructural inference, not a release assay. Catalog stages include sectioning/acquisition; analysis is volumetric reconstruction. Mitochondria were auto-detected with a network trained on manual labels (STAR Methods). Compare to Hemibrain/TEMCA2 before treating DCV distributions as cell-type canonical.

plain_language_summary: Olfactory neurons in the fly dump smell information into the learning center at swollen axon endings. Electron-microscope reconstructions split those endings into three shapes, and the most elaborate ones look best equipped to release both fast transmitters and slower chemical modulators.

ocar.opportunity: Reservoir computing uses a fixed recurrent network to lift inputs into a high-dimensional dynamical space. If real connectome topology improved reservoirs, one could both design better networks and interpret biological wiring as computation.
ocar.challenge: Standard reservoirs are random. How modularity, density, size, and other complex features affect learning is not known from simple random-graph models.
ocar.action: d’Andrea, Puppin, and De Domenico, in an arXiv preprint dated 2 November 2022 (arXiv:2211.00161), build reservoirs from synthetic graphs with varied topology and from 45 empirical connectomes spanning eight species, then test prediction on stochastic and deterministic signals.
ocar.resolution: They report nontrivial correlations of performance with node count and with the rank of the activation-state covariance matrix, with the sign depending on whether inputs are stochastic or deterministic. Modularity and link density affect performance in ways not predicted by models that keep only simple topological features. They argue complex connectome features can guide bio-inspired RNNs.
ocar.future_work: The extract’s discussion turns to using RC as a probe of structure–function in the 45-connectome set; causal interventions on modularity in vivo are not performed.

summaries.beginner: Some machine-learning networks keep a frozen tangle of loops and only train the readout. This study asks whether using real brain wiring diagrams as that tangle helps prediction, and finds that community structure and connection density matter.
summaries.intermediate: d’Andrea, Puppin, and De Domenico (arXiv, 31 October / 2 November 2022) compare reservoir computers whose internal graphs are synthetic or one of 45 connectomes from eight species. Prediction performance correlates with node number and with the rank of the activation covariance, differently for stochastic versus deterministic inputs. Modularity and link density affect error in ways simple topology models miss. Species examples in figures include Rattus and rhesus networks.
summaries.advanced: Preprint (cond-mat.dis-nn), no journal in the catalog record. ‘45 connectomes, 8 species’ is the authors’ corpus; reconstruction quality and scale differ across those graphs and are not equalized in the extract. Performance metrics (normalized MSE) should be read from figures. This is machine learning on static graphs, not a claim that brains implement echo-state computing.

plain_language_summary: Some machine-learning networks keep a frozen tangle of loops and only train the readout. This study asks whether using real brain wiring diagrams as that tangle helps prediction, and finds that community structure and connection density matter.

ocar.opportunity: Papilio xuthus has six spectral photoreceptor classes and three ommatidial types, and can discriminate 1 nm wavelength differences from UV to red—finer than human color vision. A lamina connectome could show how that precision is wired.
ocar.challenge: Drosophila early color circuits are increasingly mapped, but flower-visiting insects with richer spectral sampling need comparative synaptic data. Inter-photoreceptor wiring may differ.
ocar.action: Matsushita, Stewart, Ilić, Chen, Wakita, Miyazaki, Murata, Kinoshita, Belušič, and Arikawa, in Current Biology (2022), reconstruct the first optic ganglion (lamina) of P. xuthus, as described in the catalog abstract.
ocar.resolution: The abstract reports cartridges that typically contain nine photoreceptor axons and four second-order neurons, abundant inter-photoreceptor connections absent in the D. melanogaster lamina, connections between neighboring cartridges especially those from spectrally distinct ommatidia, and that linear summation of those synapses well explains spectral sensitivities of photoreceptors and second-order lamina neurons.
ocar.future_work: How such lamina motifs evolve across insects, and how they feed later optic neuropils, is posed as the comparative agenda.

summaries.beginner: Swallowtail butterflies see color in finer steps than people do. This paper maps the first waystation of that visual system and finds photoreceptors talking to each other in ways fruit flies lack.
summaries.intermediate: Matsushita et al. (Current Biology, 2022) present a Papilio xuthus lamina connectome. According to the catalog abstract, each cartridge usually has nine photoreceptor axons and four second-order neurons; inter-photoreceptor synapses are abundant unlike Drosophila; neighboring cartridges, especially spectrally different ones, are connected; linear summation of connections accounts for spectral sensitivities. Summaries follow the catalog abstract because the associated PDF extract is a different article.
summaries.advanced: The PDF text supplied with pdf_trust=ok is Dang, Cerkvenik, Ilić, Pirih, Debevc, Briscoe, and Belušič, Journal of Comparative Physiology A (2026), on graded opsin co-expression and spectral tuning of G+R− receptors in Heliconius melpomene, not the Matsushita et al. Papilio lamina connectome. Claims above are taken only from the catalog abstract. Independent reading of the Current Biology paper is required.

plain_language_summary: Swallowtail butterflies see color in finer steps than people do. This paper maps the first waystation of that visual system and finds photoreceptors talking to each other in ways fruit flies lack.

ocar.opportunity: Quasi-isotropic FIB-SEM can image whole cells at nanometer scale, but manual segmentation of intracellular organelles blocks routine use.
ocar.challenge: Structures span orders of magnitude in size and complexity, imaging conditions vary, and ground-truth painting is expensive.
ocar.action: Gallusser, Maltese, Di Caprio, Vadakkan, Sanyal, Somerville, Sahasrabudhe, O’Connor, Weigert, and Kirchhausen, in Journal of Cell Biology (extract; catalog bioRxiv 2022), present ASEM: dedicated convolutional models trained on sparse annotations from one or two cells, plus a fast refinement strategy that adds a few extra labels to new imaging conditions.
ocar.resolution: Models identify mitochondria, Golgi, ER, nuclear pore complexes, caveolae, and clathrin-coated pits and vesicles in FIB-SEM. They report a wide range of membrane–nuclear-pore diameters within a single cell and morphological metrics of clathrin pits and vesicles consistent with the classical constant-growth assembly model. Video legends describe successful transfer to held-out cells and mitotic ER fenestrations not present in interphase training labels.
ocar.future_work: Comparisons with CDeep3M and COSEM are tabulated in supplements; generalization still depends on occasional fine-tuning when fixation or voxel size changes.

summaries.beginner: Cell biologists can now mill and scan an entire cell in an electron microscope, but painting every organelle by hand is impractical. This pipeline trains a neural net on a little bit of human labeling and then finds mitochondria, Golgi, ER, pores, and coated vesicles automatically.
summaries.intermediate: Gallusser et al. (JCB; DOI 10.1083/jcb.202208005) introduce ASEM for segmenting intracellular structures in quasi-isotropic FIB-SEM. Each organelle gets a model trained on sparse labels from one or two cells, with a cheap refinement step for new imaging conditions. They segment mitochondria, Golgi, ER, NPCs, caveolae, and clathrin-coated pits/vesicles, and they report within-cell variation in nuclear-pore diameters plus clathrin metrics matching constant-growth assembly. Related-work contrasts CDeep3M and COSEM (Heinrich et al. 2021).
summaries.advanced: Catalog record is a 2022 bioRxiv; the extract is the JCB paper. This is cell-biological vEM segmentation, not a neuronal connectome. Performance numbers live in supplementary tables (S1–S10) not fully reproduced in the extract. False-positive mitochondria on small tubules are noted in a video legend. High-pressure freezing versus chemical fixation affects transfer and is tested rather than assumed universal.

plain_language_summary: Cell biologists can now mill and scan an entire cell in an electron microscope, but painting every organelle by hand is impractical. This pipeline trains a neural net on a little bit of human labeling and then finds mitochondria, Golgi, ER, pores, and coated vesicles automatically.

ocar.opportunity: Genetic tools, tethered and free behavior, physiology, and connectomics now let Drosophila visual behaviors be traced from photons to actions at identified cells.
ocar.challenge: Features such as brightness, color, local motion, optic flow, and translating or approaching objects are processed in parallel pathways whose central-brain targets serve different jobs.
ocar.action: Ryu, Kim, and Kim, in Frontiers in Neuroscience (published 4 May 2022), review how those features are detected and converted into phototaxis, optomotor responses, object attraction or aversion, navigation, and visual learning.
ocar.resolution: They organize central projections: some optic glomeruli drive descending neurons for fast reflexes; AOTU preserves more retinotopy toward the central complex for heading and navigation; medulla–mushroom-body paths support visual learning. They note Marr–Poggio multi-level analysis and cite connectomic work on central-complex heading algorithms later confirmed physiologically.
ocar.future_work: Behaviors whose circuits are still thin, including vision-based gap distance estimation, are flagged as incomplete. They ask whether implementation-level maps will keep yielding new algorithms.

summaries.beginner: Fruit flies turn what they see into walks, turns, chases, and memories. This review walks through the known neural paths from the eye to those actions, now sharpened by wiring diagrams.
summaries.intermediate: Ryu, Kim, and Kim (Frontiers in Neuroscience, 2022) review Drosophila visual feature detection and downstream behavior: phototaxis, optomotor response, object approach/avoidance, navigation, and visual learning. They contrast optic-glomerulus descending reflexes, a more retinotopic AOTU route into the central complex, and a medulla–mushroom-body learning path. The discussion invokes Marr and Poggio and treats recent CX connectomics as an example of implementation informing algorithm.
summaries.advanced: Narrative review, not new data. Coverage is explicitly ‘comprehensive but hardly complete.’ Gap-crossing distance estimation is an example of a behavior with only partial circuit knowledge. Catalog axis is infrastructure; the paper is a systems-vision review that uses connectomes as evidence.

plain_language_summary: Fruit flies turn what they see into walks, turns, chases, and memories. This review walks through the known neural paths from the eye to those actions, now sharpened by wiring diagrams.

ocar.opportunity: Connectome research has grown since 2005. A bibliometric map could show which journals, countries, and topics dominate, and what is rising.
ocar.challenge: Narrative reviews rarely quantify the literature. Dual-database retrieval and topic modeling are needed to see hotspots without reading every paper.
ocar.action: Yan, Fan, Liao, and Zhao, in Frontiers in Neuroscience (published 22 December 2022), search Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus for connectom* (2005–2021), analyze the corpus in R/bibliometrix, and apply latent Dirichlet allocation. Retrieval date 24 October 2022.
ocar.resolution: They include 14,140 publications. NeuroImage ranks first by volume (1,427 articles) and by h-index (122). Most papers come from developed countries, led by the United States; Harvard Medical School and the University of Pennsylvania are the two most productive institutions. Two major LDA topics are neuroimaging analysis technology and brain functions and diseases. Trends include machine learning, deep learning, graph theory, and dynamic functional connectivity; alcohol-use disorder and migraine appear as connectivity topics in the last two years of the window.
ocar.future_work: The study is a snapshot through 2021 of mostly large-scale MRI/EEG/MEG connectomics; it does not evaluate experimental quality of individual papers.

summaries.beginner: This paper counts two decades of ‘connectome’ publications instead of dissecting one experiment. Imaging journals and U.S. institutions lead, and computer methods plus disease studies are the two big themes.
summaries.intermediate: Yan et al. (Frontiers in Neuroscience, 2022) bibliometrically analyze 14,140 WoS and Scopus records (2005–2021). NeuroImage leads in count (1,427) and h-index (122). The United States leads nationally; Harvard Medical School and University of Pennsylvania lead among institutions. LDA yields neuroimaging-methods versus brain-function/disease topics. Recent keywords include ML/DL, graph theory, dynamic FC, and, in the last two years, alcohol-use disorder and migraine.
summaries.advanced: Bibliometrics measures attention, not scientific validity. Search term connectom* mixes microscale EM and human MRI. h-index 122 is journal-level in this field subset as computed by the authors. The extract’s tail is methods (search strings), not a full discussion of limitations such as English-language or database bias, though no language filter is stated.

ocar.opportunity: Saturated reconstruction of brain tissue has been an EM privilege on dead samples. Live super-resolution light microscopy could add time, activity, and molecular labels if photo-burden, bleaching, 3-D resolution, and SNR could be solved together.
ocar.challenge: STED and related methods have not previously delivered complete, synapse-level 3-D reconstructions of living neuropil without wrecking the tissue.
ocar.action: Velicky, Miguel, Michalska, Wei, Lin, Watson, Troidl, Beyer, Ben-Simon, Sommer, Jahr, Cenameri, Broichhagen, Grant, Jonas, Novarino, Pfister, Bickel, and Danzl, in a bioRxiv preprint (this version 9 May 2022), combine extracellular labeling, adapted STED (LIONESS), and a two-stage deep-learning reconstruction that reuses prior structural information to cut dose.
ocar.resolution: They demonstrate saturated reconstruction of living brain tissue down to synapses, with molecular context (e.g., PSD95 and synaptophysin) and calcium imaging (GCaMP) in organotypic mouse hippocampal cultures, including mossy-fiber boutons. Automated segmentation is used; some neighboring boutons in videos are not proofread.
ocar.future_work: The authors present the stack as an adoptable technology for relating architecture to activity and targeted activation over time. Extent of proofreading versus automation should be checked in the full paper.

summaries.beginner: Wiring diagrams from electron microscopes are snapshots of dead tissue. This preprint shows a super-resolution light method that reconstructs living brain tissue down to synapses while cells still fire.
summaries.intermediate: Velicky et al. (bioRxiv, 9 May 2022) introduce LIONESS: extracellularly labeled living tissue imaged with adapted STED, then reconstructed with two-stage deep learning that exploits known sample structure to reduce photo-burden. They report saturated, synapse-level volumes in mouse organotypic hippocampus, overlay molecular labels (PSD95, synaptophysin), and pair structure with GCaMP (including gabazine and DREADD-activated mossy-fiber boutons). Step sizes in videos are 50 nm.
summaries.advanced: Preprint, not peer-reviewed in this extract. ‘Saturated’ is the authors’ claim for the imaged volumes, not whole-brain completeness. Some automatic bouton reconstructions are explicitly not proofread (Supplementary Video 8). Catalog dataset tag DS11 Kasthuri neocortex does not match these live hippocampal cultures. Compare to any later journal version for phototoxicity limits and error rates.

plain_language_summary: Wiring diagrams from electron microscopes are snapshots of dead tissue. This preprint shows a super-resolution light method that reconstructs living brain tissue down to synapses while cells still fire.

ocar.opportunity: Neuronal stem-cell lineages are developmental units; circuits are functional units. Mapping how temporal cohorts from different lineages join into a motif would show a developmental logic of wiring.
ocar.challenge: It is unclear whether connectivity follows an early-to-early, late-to-late rule or some other birth-order program, especially across lineages.
ocar.action: Wang, Wreden, Levy, Marshall, MacLean, and Heckscher, in a 6 April 2022 bioRxiv preprint, combine Twin-spot MARCM (optimized for embryos/early larvae), Multi-color Flip Out, permanent labeling, calcium imaging, the Drosophila larval connectome, and network analyses.
ocar.resolution: Many lineages form temporal cohorts whose boundaries match sharp changes in input connectivity. A feed-forward motif that encodes vibration-onset is assembled by preferential links among temporal cohorts from different stem-cell lineages. Output neurons are born before input neurons—sequential addition, not early-to-early matching. They release tools including an NB3-3 lineage with birth order, morphology, and input connectivity at single-neuron/synapse precision, a new NB3-3-GAL4, and methods linking anatomy to developmental origin (neurite bundles, cortex neurite length).
ocar.future_work: They propose sequential addition (oldest outputs, youngest inputs) as a candidate general strategy for feed-forward circuits. Molecular predictions (e.g., Castor in late-born ELs) remain to be tested.

summaries.beginner: Nerve-cord circuits in the fly larva are built in birth-order batches. In the vibration-onset circuit studied here, the cells that send the answer are born before the cells that bring the news—the opposite of a simple old-wires-to-old-wires rule.
summaries.intermediate: Wang, Wreden, Levy, Marshall, MacLean, and Heckscher (bioRxiv, 6 April 2022) show that Drosophila larval lineages organize as temporal cohorts with sharp input-connectivity transitions. A feed-forward vibration-onset motif forms by sequential addition of cohorts across lineages, with outputs older than inputs. Methods include embryonic ts-MARCM, MCFO, calcium imaging, and larval connectome analyses. Resources include fully birth-ordered NB3-3A1L/R and a new NB3-3-GAL4.
summaries.advanced: Preprint. ‘Many lineages’ is qualitative; counts of lineages scored are in the full figures. Connectome-based birth-order proxies (cortex neurite length) are validated against genetics but remain approximations. Catalog dataset DS03 Drosophila larva matches. All rights reserved on this bioRxiv license line—reuse restricted.

ocar.opportunity: Deeper layers of auditory systems have not been fully mapped in any model animal. Drosophila now combines behavior, physiology, genetics, and whole-brain EM.
ocar.challenge: There is a tradeoff between detailed circuit knowledge and brain-wide descriptions of activity; few systems can do both at synaptic resolution.
ocar.action: Bates and Jefferis, in a Current Biology dispatch (2022), preview a study that links comprehensive connectomics of Drosophila song-perception circuits to physiological response profiles, as described in the catalog abstract.
ocar.resolution: The abstract states that the new study connects a full-ish wiring diagram of fly song-perception circuitry to response profiles. Identifiable fragments in a scrambled extract argue that Drosophila investigators can now ask systems-level questions with whole-brain connectomics, defining a wave of synaptic-resolution systems neuroscience that will spread to other models—‘Roeder would surely approve.’
ocar.future_work: The dispatch’s agenda is that this style of work should extend beyond flies; it does not itself map vertebrate auditory hindbrain.

summaries.beginner: Hearing pathways deep in the brain have never been fully wired in any animal. This short commentary highlights a fly study that pairs a song-circuit wiring diagram with how the cells actually fire.
summaries.intermediate: Bates and Jefferis (Current Biology, 2022) write a dispatch on synaptic-resolution auditory processing in Drosophila. The catalog abstract says a new study links comprehensive connectomics of song-perception circuits to physiological profiles. Summaries follow the abstract, with only clearly matching commentary sentences used, because the associated PDF extract is mixed with another paper.
summaries.advanced: The PDF extract is not a clean copy of this dispatch: the head is references from a different Current Biology piece (sexual antagonism / local adaptation), while two-column leftovers include Bates/Jefferis prose on Drosophila audition, connectomics, and Roeder. Claims above use the catalog abstract plus those matching sentences only. Read the publisher HTML/PDF directly. This is a preview, not primary connectomics.
